The Future of End-User Computing: Automation & Modernisation Focused  
   
  Permanent Full-Time Role | Melbourne-based  
   
 This is not your typical desktop support or Level 2 Service Desk role. We are looking for an ambitious future superstar ready to grow beyond ticket-churning support into a trusted advisor who understands people, processes, and technology. This role is built for engineers who are passionate about modernisation and have a core mentality of "doing work once" by embracing automation and continuous improvement. 
   
  The Opportunity  
   
 Join a team dedicated to transforming the end-user workplace experience. You will be instrumental in designing, building, and maintaining a secure and highly automated modern workplace environment. You will apply your deep technical expertise to lead modernisation projects that deliver seamless, proactive, and efficient technology experiences to all users. 
   
  Key Responsibilities  
 
   Automation & Scripting Leadership:    Drive the automation of Workplace Technology tasks using proficiency in PowerShell, Bash Shell, and Microsoft Graph API  . Oversee application lifecycle management, including packaging, deployment, updating, and retirement of apps.  
   Endpoint Management:    Manage endpoints across Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android using industry-leading MDM solutions, primarily Microsoft Intune and JAMF.  
   Advanced Troubleshooting:    Act as a senior escalation point for complex Level 2-3 endpoint, hardware, and application issues, utilising diagnostic tools and structured methodologies to perform Root Cause Analysis (RCA).  
   Cloud & Virtual Desktop:    Support and administer Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) environments  ,   including host pool configuration, FSLogix profile management, Azure Workspaces, and integration with Microsoft cloud infrastructure  .  
   Policy & Compliance:    Adeptly enforce policies, automate workflows, manage Standard Operating Environments (SOE's), and support operations.  
   Monitoring & Reporting:    Monitor and report on endpoint health using tools like Intune, Endpoint Analytics, and Power BI, generating continuous insights and trends through automated dashboards.  
   Unified Communications:    Administer unified communications and conferencing systems such as Microsoft Teams Calling and Cisco Webex, ensuring reliable operation and performance.  
   Documentation & Mentorship:    Document configurations and share knowledge via platforms like Confluence and Jira  , and provide guidance and mentorship to junior members of the team, acting as a Subject Matter Expert (SME). 
   
 
   Asset Management:    Manage hardware and software assets, tracking inventory, overseeing procurement, and ensuring licensing and audit compliance.  
 
  What You'll Bring  
 
  A resourceful and confident specialist with a passion for new technologies and a bias towards proactivity and prevention.  
  Proven experience in a Technical Lead or senior support role within an Enterprise-level environment.  
  A natural talent for recognizing problem patterns and streamlining processes to continuously improve the end-user experience.  
  Strong technical communication and customer focus with the ability to translate complex information for non-technical users.  
 
  Technical Expertise  
 
   Modern Device Management:    Expertise in Microsoft Intune (including Intune Suite), Endpoint Manager, policies, compliance, and app deployment.  
   Deployment Tools:    Strong hands-on experience with Windows Autopilot and INTUNE enrollment  .   Experience with co-management using Configuration Manager (SCCM/MECM)  .  
   Windows Ecosystem:    Deep engineering knowledge of Microsoft technologies, including Windows Hello, Active Directory, Group Policy, and Microsoft Entra ID (Azure Identity).  
   Application Packaging:    Advanced experience with application packaging, deployment, and testing, including creating and managing complex packages (e.g., Win32, MSI, MSIX, LOB apps).  
   Automation & Scripting:    Proficiency in automation and Device Lifecycle Management using scripting techniques (PowerShell, Bash) and tools such as Power Automate and Power Apps.  
   Cloud Infrastructure:    Expertise in implementing, administering, and monitoring Azure Virtual Desktop environments and associated cloud services.

Sunquest Signs
Project Administrator (Client Manager)
33 Technology Dr, Warana QLD 4575
Full-Time | Permanent
$135,000 per annum plus Superannuation
 
Welcome to Sunquest Signs
Sunquest Signs is a well-established Australian signage company delivering high-quality signage solutions across commercial, industrial, government and infrastructure sectors.
We specialise in designing, manufacturing and installing custom signage solutions while building long-term relationships through exceptional customer service, technical expertise and professional project delivery.
As our business continues to expand into new markets, we are seeking an experienced Project Administrator (Client Manager) to coordinate multiple signage projects from initial client consultation through to successful project completion.
This is a senior professional position responsible for project planning, commercial coordination, client relationship management and operational administration, ensuring projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on schedule and within budget.
 
About the Role
Reporting directly to senior management, the Project Administrator (Client Manager) is responsible for planning, coordinating and administering multiple concurrent signage projects throughout the complete project lifecycle.
The role requires responsibility for coordinating project schedules, allocating resources, monitoring budgets, preparing estimates, managing client communication, coordinating production and installation activities, maintaining project documentation and ensuring compliance with company procedures and workplace legislation.
The successful applicant will play a key role in ensuring commercial success while maintaining exceptional client service and operational excellence.
 
Key Responsibilities
Project Planning & Administration
•	Plan, coordinate and administer multiple signage projects from commencement through to completion. 
•	Develop detailed project schedules and implementation plans. 
•	Coordinate project activities across design, production, procurement and installation teams. 
•	Monitor project milestones and ensure deliverables are achieved within agreed timelines. 
•	Maintain comprehensive project documentation and administrative records. 
•	Monitor project performance and recommend corrective actions where required. 
•	Coordinate internal resources and external contractors to optimise project delivery. 
•	Prepare project reports for management and clients. 
Client Relationship Management
•	Manage client enquiries from initial consultation through to project completion. 
•	Interpret client specifications and project requirements. 
•	Develop and maintain strong professional relationships with clients, consultants and stakeholders. 
•	Coordinate client meetings, project updates and approval processes. 
•	Manage project variations and changes to project scope. 
•	Resolve project issues professionally while maintaining exceptional customer service. 
Commercial Administration & Estimating
•	Prepare accurate quotations, cost estimates and project proposals. 
•	Assess project specifications, labour requirements, materials and production costs. 
•	Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets. 
•	Maintain agreed gross profit margins. 
•	Coordinate purchase orders, project costing and final invoicing through Xero. 
•	Assist management with commercial planning, pricing strategies and profitability analysis. 
Production & Design Coordination
•	Coordinate artwork development and client approval processes. 
•	Prepare production-ready artwork for manufacture or approved external suppliers. 
•	Liaise closely with production personnel to ensure technical accuracy. 
•	Coordinate manufacturing schedules and installation programs. 
•	Ensure quality standards are maintained throughout project delivery. 
Site Coordination & Compliance
•	Conduct site inspections and site measurements where required. 
•	Prepare Job Safety Analyses (JSA) and Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS). 
•	Ensure compliance with Workplace Health and Safety legislation and company procedures. 
•	Maintain accurate compliance documentation throughout each project. 
•	Coordinate installation activities to minimise project risk and maximise efficiency. 
Business Development
•	Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships. 
•	Develop new business opportunities across emerging industry sectors. 
•	Build relationships with architects, builders, developers, consultants and commercial clients. 
•	Support strategic growth initiatives and diversification into new market segments. 
•	Contribute to the ongoing development of Sunquest Signs' client portfolio. 
 
Benefits & Remuneration
Sunquest Signs offers:
•	Competitive salary of $135,000 per annum plus Superannuation 
•	Quarterly and annual performance-based commission incentives 
•	Fuel card ($100 per week business allowance) 
•	Company mobile phone 
•	Four weeks annual leave 
•	Long-term career opportunity within a growing Australian business 
•	Supportive and collaborative leadership team 
•	Professional development opportunities 
 
Qualifications & Experience
Applicants should possess:
•	A relevant tertiary qualification in Project Management, Construction Management, Business, Engineering, Design, Manufacturing or another closely related discipline, or equivalent relevant industry experience. 
•	Minimum three years' experience coordinating commercial projects in a similar environment: signage, manufacturing, construction, engineering or a related technical industry. 
•	Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple concurrent projects. 
•	Experience preparing commercial quotations and project estimates. 
•	Experience coordinating project schedules, budgets and resources. 
•	Experience liaising with clients, contractors and suppliers. 
•	Experience using project management software. 
•	Experience using Xero is highly regarded. 
•	Current Australian Driver's Licence or ability to obtain one. 
 
Skills
The successful applicant will demonstrate:
•	Exceptional project planning and coordination skills. 
•	Strong commercial and financial acumen. 
•	Excellent organisational and time management abilities. 
•	Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. 
•	Excellent stakeholder and client relationship management. 
•	High attention to detail and accuracy. 
•	Strong analytical and problem-solving capability. 
•	Ability to prioritise competing deadlines. 
•	Ability to coordinate multidisciplinary teams. 
•	Strong understanding of project documentation and compliance. 
•	Commitment to continuous improvement and professional excellence. 
•	Commitment to workplace health, safety and quality management systems. 
 
Performance Expectations
Success in this role will be measured by:
Commercial Performance
•	Achievement of quarterly and annual sales objectives. 
•	Maintenance of agreed gross profit margins. 
•	Accurate project estimating and financial performance. 
Project Delivery
•	Projects completed safely, on time and within budget. 
•	Effective coordination of project resources. 
•	Minimal production errors or rework. 
•	Accurate project administration and documentation. 
Client Satisfaction
•	High levels of customer satisfaction. 
•	Strong client retention and repeat business. 
•	Professional communication throughout each project. 
Team Contribution
•	Positive collaboration with production, installation and management teams. 
•	Compliance with company systems and operational procedures. 
•	Contribution to continuous improvement initiatives.
$135,000 per annum plus Superannuation

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




About the Department - Program 


Join Monash Health as a Quality Systems & Insights Analyst and play a key role in improving the safety and quality of care for one of Victoria's largest health services. Combining data analytics, quality systems expertise and clinical governance insight, you'll transform information into meaningful action, support organisation wide quality systems, and help leaders make decisions that improve patient outcomes. If you enjoy solving problems, working with data, optimising systems, and partnering with stakeholders to drive continuous improvement and positive change, this is an opportunity to make a real impact across a complex and dynamic healthcare environment.


The Quality & Clinical Governance Unit plays a central role in supporting Monash Health's commitment to delivering safe, effective and high-quality care. The team provides leadership, systems and oversight that strengthen clinical governance, quality improvement, patient safety and organisational learning across the health service.


The Quality Insights & Systems team manages and optimises key quality systems, supports the collection and analysis of clinical governance information, and provides meaningful insights that help leaders identify risks, monitor performance and drive continuous improvement. Working collaboratively with programs and services across Monash Health, the team supports evidence-based decision-making and initiatives that enhance patient outcomes and organisational performance.







About the Role 








This is a part time ongoing position located at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, you will work under the leadership of the Quality Insights & Systems manager and collaborate closely with the broader Quality & Clinical Governance team and stakeholders across Monash Health.


This is an exciting opportunity for a quality systems and data professional who enjoys combining analytical thinking, systems administration and continuous improvement to support safer patient care. Administering and optimising Monash Health's quality systems, including incident management, document control and audit platforms.


Analysing clinical quality data and other information sources to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement.

Providing user support, education and training to improve staff capability in quality systems and data interpretation. 


Working with internal stakeholders, external vendors and partner teams to enhance system performance, data integrity and governance processes. 


Contributing to quality improvement initiatives, system enhancements and process optimisation projects.









This role will involve working with stakeholders across multiple Monash Health sites. A hybrid working arrangement may be available in line with team and organisational requirements.







About You 


To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring demonstrated experience in systems administration, data analysis and quality improvement within a complex organisational environment. 


You will be someone who is curious, analytical and solutions-focused, with the ability to translate data into meaningful insights and build strong collaborative relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.


You will have:




Experience administering, supporting or improving systems and processes in a complex organisation. 


Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends and communicate actionable insights. 


Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including report writing, presentations and development of guidance materials.


Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-building capabilities. 


Experience providing education, training and support to end-users.


High attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining data integrity and quality. 


Demonstrated problem-solving skills and a continuous improvement mindset. 


Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.


Experience using RiskMan, PROMPT, MARS or similar systems will be highly regarded.

The Opportunity
The School of Computer Science and Engineering has an opportunity for a two-year fixed term Postdoctoral Fellow in Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence. This Level A position is expected to conduct research in Neuro-Symbolic AI for reasoning and decision-making, contributing to UNSW’s research effort and developing expertise through defined projects.

This position offers the opportunity to advance your scholarly research and professional activities on both national and international levels. You will contribute to the writing of scientific papers and reports for international journals, participate in conferences and workshops, supervise HDR students, and actively collaborate with industry partners.

This role reports to Associate Professor Yang Song and has no direct reports. 

•	Salary, Level A - AUD$95,036 to $126,711 per annum + 17% superannuation
•	Full time
•	Fixed-term contract – 2 years (with the possibility of one-year extension) 
•	Location: Kensington – Sydney, Australia

About UNSW
UNSW is a world leading institution recognised for its scale, prestige, and impact. With strong industry engagement and partnerships across sectors, UNSW provides a unique environment where academic expertise translates into real world outcomes. The university is home to cutting edge research that drives innovation and societal progress, while its excellence in teaching ensures students are prepared to lead in their fields. For academics, UNSW offers an outstanding platform to flourish — combining world class facilities, collaborative networks, and a culture of innovation that supports both career growth and meaningful contributions to the wider community.

The School of Computer Science and Engineering is one of the largest and most prestigious schools of computing in Australia. It offers undergraduate programmes in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, and Bioinformatics, as well as a number of combined degrees with other disciplines. Our research and teaching staff are world leading and world building as they advance knowledge and learning. For more information on our school go to the following link - https://www.unsw.edu.au/engineering/our-schools/computer-science-and-engineering 

Skills and Experience
• PhD (or soon to be awarded) in computer science and artificial intelligence.
• Strong knowledge and research outputs in AI, particularly in the field of deep learning, knowledge representation and reasoning, or neuro-symbolic AI.
• Proven commitment to proactively keeping up to date with discipline knowledge and developments.
• Demonstrated ability to undertake high quality academic research and conduct independent research with limited supervision.
• Demonstrated track record of publications and conference presentations relative to opportunity.
• Demonstrated ability to work in a team, collaborate across disciplines and build effective relationships.
• Evidence of highly developed interpersonal skills.
• Demonstrated ability to communicate and interact with a diverse range of stakeholders and students.
• An understanding of and commitment to UNSW’s aims, objectives and values in action, together with relevant policies and guidelines.

result.description: Mega HVAC Pty Ltd  Our commitment to quality, innovation, and exceptional customer service has earned us a strong reputation within the industry. With modern manufacturing facilities in Oakleigh, Victoria, and a portfolio that includes major projects such as Footscray Hospital, the University of Melbourne, Chadstone Shopping Centre, and Melbourne Quarter, we continue to support Australia's growing construction sector with reliable, high-quality HVAC solutions.     As our business continues to expand, we are seeking a qualified Welder to join our skilled fabrication team and contribute to the delivery of premium HVAC products.      KEY TASKS    Interpret engineering drawings, fabrication plans, and technical specifications to prepare and weld customised HVAC ductwork and sheet metal components in accordance with project requirements.  Determine appropriate welding techniques, materials, joint configurations, and fabrication sequences to ensure structural integrity, dimensional accuracy, and compliance with manufacturing specifications.  Perform MIG and TIG welding on galvanised steel, stainless steel, and other sheet metal materials used in the manufacture of rectangular, spiral, and oval HVAC duct systems.  Fabricate, assemble, and weld sheet metal ductwork, fittings, supports, frames, and associated HVAC components.  Set up, operate, and maintain welding equipment, hand tools, and fabrication machinery to achieve accurate welds while ensuring safe and efficient production.  Inspect weld preparations, fit-up, alignment, and completed welds to verify compliance with engineering drawings, quality standards, and Australian manufacturing requirements.  Finish welded assemblies by grinding, dressing, deburring, and polishing welds to achieve the required surface quality, dimensional tolerances, and presentation standards.  Collaborate with fabrication and production teams to resolve welding and fabrication issues, ensuring projects are completed efficiently and within scheduled production timelines. result.description:
Senior Property, Power & Construction Underwriter
Asia Mideast Insurance and Reinsurance Pty Ltd
Location: North Sydney NSW 2060
Employment Type: Full-time
Position: Senior Property, Power & Construction Underwriter


About the Business
Asia Mideast Insurance and Reinsurance Pty Ltd, known as AMIR, is an underwriting agency and Lloyd’s of London Coverholder based in North Sydney, New South Wales.
AMIR focuses on underwriting insurance and reinsurance risks, with particular expertise in complex and specialty risks in Australia and overseas. The business actively underwrites risks across Australia, New Zealand, the Middle East, Asia, Africa and the Indian sub-continent.
AMIR has been operating successfully for 28 years and has developed a strong reputation for technical underwriting expertise, profitable underwriting results, responsive broker service and long-standing relationships across international insurance and reinsurance markets.


About the Role
AMIR is seeking a full time Senior Property, Power & Construction Underwriter to join its North Sydney office.
The successful candidate will be responsible for underwriting property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance risks across Australian and international markets. The role requires advanced technical underwriting capability, strong commercial judgement, experience in high risk property, power and construction exposures, and the ability to work closely with insurance and reinsurance brokers, cedants, capacity providers and internal stakeholders.
This is a senior technical underwriting role which will involve risk assessment, pricing, broker liaison, portfolio development, risk mitigation planning, review of survey and loss information, and training of junior underwriting staff.


Key Duties and Responsibilities
The Senior Property, Power & Construction Underwriter will be responsible for:
•	Underwriting property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance risks in accordance with AMIR’s underwriting authorities, binder requirements and internal procedures. 
•	Assessing complex property, power and construction risks, including exposure, construction type, occupancy, location, loss history, survey findings, policy terms, risk mitigation measures and underwriting suitability. 
•	Reviewing and analysing risk survey reports, engineering information, loss records, policy wordings, slips, endorsements and supporting underwriting documentation. 
•	Preparing underwriting recommendations, pricing, terms, conditions and coverage positions for property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance risks. 
•	Developing technical underwriting plans to manage high-risk exposures across property, power and construction classes of business. 
•	Applying risk modelling techniques and relevant risk assessment tools to evaluate exposure, probable loss and underwriting acceptability. 
•	Reviewing applicable sanctions, territorial issues and compliance considerations relevant to international insurance and reinsurance risks. 
•	Liaising with insurance and reinsurance brokers in Australia and overseas to obtain underwriting information, clarify risk details and negotiate appropriate terms. 
•	Developing and maintaining strong relationships with insurance and reinsurance brokers to support quality business submissions and long term portfolio development. 
•	Attending relevant industry seminars, conferences and market meetings in Australia and overseas. 
•	Undertaking business travel as required to meet insurance and reinsurance brokers, promote AMIR’s underwriting capabilities and increase appropriate business opportunities. 
•	Liaising with loss adjusters and relevant professional advisers in relation to major property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance losses. 
•	Applying Lloyd’s of London risk codes, reporting expectations and underwriting requirements where relevant. 
•	Supporting portfolio monitoring, renewal reviews, underwriting performance analysis and internal reporting. 
•	Training and mentoring an Assistant Underwriter appointed from the Australian market in underwriting processes, broker liaison, risk assessment and business development matters. 


Skills and Experience Required
The successful applicant will be expected to have:
•	Minimum 10 years’ underwriting experience in property, power and construction insurance and/or reinsurance. 
•	Minimum 7 years’ experience underwriting property, power and construction risks in the Middle East. 
•	Demonstrated experience in underwriting high-risk property, power and construction exposures. 
•	Strong familiarity with risk mitigation measures for complex insurance and reinsurance exposures. 
•	Experience using risk modelling techniques and relevant tools for property, power and construction risk assessment. 
•	Strong relationships with insurance and reinsurance brokers across international markets, excluding USA and Canada. 
•	Familiarity with sanctions regimes applicable to international insurance and reinsurance risks. 
•	Ability to review risk survey reports and identify relevant underwriting information required for proper risk assessment. 
•	Experience dealing with international loss adjusting firms in relation to large property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance losses. 
•	Familiarity with Lloyd’s of London risk codes, binder requirements and underwriting standards. 
•	Ability to train junior underwriting staff in technical underwriting, broker liaison and business development matters. 
•	Academic engineering knowledge or engineering-related qualifications to support technical risk assessment. 
•	Proven track record of profitable underwriting results. 
•	Strong written and verbal communication skills. 
•	High level attention to detail and ability to work accurately within underwriting guidelines, binder requirements and compliance obligations. 
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant underwriting, reporting, risk assessment or risk modelling systems. 


Qualifications
Relevant qualifications in insurance, reinsurance, engineering, risk management, business, finance or a related field will be highly regarded.
Professional Insurance qualification minimum Diploma in Insurance from the Chartered Insurance Institute in UK, or Australian equivalent. 


How to Apply
Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant property, power and construction underwriting experience.
Applications should be sent to: adel@amir.com.au
